title: Replying to @Landon so did I like it (spam)a lot or (spam)a little?  ...
transcript: Last night I saw the first preview of Monty Python’s Spamalot, so let's talk about it! So I actually got to see the original production of Spamalot twice on Broadway and I was obsessed with it when it came out- I listened to the cast recording all the time! So I was really excited for this new production and to see how it compared. But I was also a little bit nervous, because the original production was actually pretty extravagant and this is a transfer of a concert production, which tends to be more minimal. And to be honest, that is very noticeable when watching this production, and I think my biggest disappointment with this revival. Other concert productions, like Into the Woods and Parade, have been able to transfer successfully and work for me in a Broadway setting, because I felt like their minimalism was able to enhance the material. But with Spamalot, there's not much depth to mine, it's just comedy. And while the comedy can still shine, without the spectacle it does lose something. There are several moments in the show where they mention spectacle in the script- like they'll mention a dark and very expensive forest, or they'll say “I can't believe you're floating with no strings or visible support device” only the forest doesn't look very expensive and you can very visibly see the supporting device that the cast member is just sitting on. For what the show lacks in set and spectacle, it certainly makes up for in performances, because the actors are so great across the board. This is a cast stacked with Broadway comedy pros and it shows! They are all at the top of their game, and I laughed so so many times, even at jokes that I've heard a million times before. This production also allows the cast to ad-lib quite a bit, and some of my favourite moments of the show last night were when the cast were able to just ad lib and make it their own and just do something completely wild and try to make everyone else on stage laugh. I also thought a lot of the design work outside of the set was really well done. Some really great lighting, and some really great costumes, although the costumes are for the most part exact recreations of the original costumes. They did update the script a little bit with modern references so there are references to Grindr and George Santos and Lea Michele, all of which are pretty funny. But (and I hate to keep harping on this) I could not stop focusing on how cheap the set looked 😅 and I think why I harp on this so much is because the rest of the production is really great! The cast is really great, it's super funny, the costumes are great, I just wish they had invested the money into getting a proper set and given us the proper Spamalot revival that we deserve, especially since this is open-ended and not a limited engagement. So should you see this production? For me it depends, if you are someone that looks for spectacle in your theater then probably not, but if you go in knowing what you're getting, which is a minimalist, but really fun and really funny Spamalot revival, I think you'll have a good time. I don't know if it's worth top Broadway ticket prices, but it's certainly a fun night out, especially if you never got to see the original production!
reasoning: The reviewer enjoyed the performances and comedy but was disappointed by the minimal set design. Despite significant reservations about the production values, they still recommend it with caveats about expectations and ticket prices.
